title: Ali, caliph
hookLine: Ali accepts the caliphate in a divided city, the fourth caliph for Sunnis, the first Imam for Shia

cards: Who wants a crown the day after the last man wearing it was murdered? Medina is in shock. The rebels are still in the streets, and the city needs someone to lead it, today.
The people go to one man's door: Ali ibn Abi Talib, the Prophet's cousin, raised in his house, married to his daughter Fatimah. And the reports say his first answer was no.
Leave me, he tells them, find someone else; I would rather be your helper than your ruler. They keep coming back.

teach.b: In the end, the histories say, Ali agreed, on one condition: the pledge would be made openly, in the mosque, where everyone could see.
So he became caliph in a divided city, and some companions held back from pledging at all. Here Muslims tell the same story two ways, and both deserve to be heard plainly.
For Sunni Muslims, Ali is the fourth of the rightly guided caliphs, after Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman, each chosen in turn, all four honored.
For Shia Muslims, Ali is the first Imam, the one the Prophet named to lead after him, and the three before him held an office that was rightfully his. Same man, same day, two counts.
Both traditions keep one saying about him.

In Bukhari's telling, when the Prophet left Ali behind in Medina during a campaign, Ali was unhappy, and the Prophet said: are you not content to be to me as Aaron was to Moses, except that there will be no prophet after me?
Shia collections carry it too. And the saying from Ghadir Khumm, met earlier, returns with new weight: of whomever I am the mawla, Ali is his mawla.
A word of love and loyalty, in the Sunni reading; an appointment to lead, in the Shia reading. Either way, the man who took up the office that day was not taking a prize.
He was taking on a fitnah already burning, and a community that would not agree on how to count him.

how: Sunni Muslims honor Ali as the fourth rightly guided caliph; Shia Muslims honor him as the first Imam, appointed by the Prophet, and both remember the hadith of Aaron and Moses about him.

games.q: you're Ali. Uthman has just been killed. the people crowd your door and ask you to lead. what do you say?
o: yes, at once, before anyone else claims it.
no, then yes, but only with an open pledge in the mosque.
games.why: the reports say he refused first, then agreed on the condition that the pledge be public, in the mosque.

practice: Bring to mind one hard duty left at the door in the hope someone else will pick it up: a difficult conversation, the care of an aging parent, the project nobody wants.
You don't have to finish it; just choose one first step you could take openly, where it can be counted on. If you pray, you can ask for strength for the duty.

wordCard.voice: Ali. Ali ibn Abi Talib, the Prophet's cousin and son-in-law: the fourth rightly guided caliph for Sunni Muslims, and the first Imam for Shia Muslims. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the name Ali, as written in the hadith collections and the histories.

carryVoice: Your line: the fourth; the first. Both counts honor the same man. Day eight hundred eighty-one.
